_comment: Worcester, MA-CT MSA — Worcester County MA plus the Connecticut portion (historically Windham County, now the Northeastern Connecticut Planning Region). Ingested from the ChatGPT Work research workbook 2026-08-03 as part of wave 1 of the v2.0 methodology. NOT YET IMPORTED. `expected_publish` is deliberately ABSENT: for a new metro the projected split IS the finding the owner needs, so it is reported by --stage=project rather than asserted.
_workbook_comment: Research methodology v2.0 — the tab override is load-bearing. v2.0 splits the human research artifact from the machine handoff: the 15 human tabs are unchanged and a new generated `Import Contract` tab is now the ONLY machine input. This workbook is generation A by tab layout, so detectGeneration() would read generation A's default primary tab `Import Ready`, which v2.0 demotes to a human-readable view. Reading a human tab as machine input is the Huntsville defect class. applyTabOverrides() ABORTS on a missing named tab rather than falling back silently.
_envelope_comment: Derived from the MSA COUNTY LIST, not the observed venue bbox (Toledo precedent). SPANS TWO STATES, so `states` lists both and the envelope must hold both sides of the state line. Extents from the US Census TIGERweb State_County service: Worcester County MA lat 42.008053..42.721615 lng -72.315879..-71.478027. THE CONNECTICUT SIDE NEEDED A DIFFERENT LOOKUP AND THIS IS WORTH RECORDING: Connecticut abolished its counties as statistical units and the Census now delineates the state by PLANNING REGION, so a TIGERweb query for 'Windham County, CT' returns an extent of literal NaN rather than an error — a silent wrong answer if coerced without checking. The Connecticut portion of this MSA is the Northeastern Connecticut Planning Region, lat 41.505704..42.031069 lng -72.234898..-71.787239, which is what the union below actually uses. Rounded OUTWARD to 0.01 deg.
msa: Worcester, MA-CT (Worcester County MA; Northeastern Connecticut Planning Region, formerly Windham County CT)
_geocode_comment: 23 of 24 venues geocoded (22 high precision, 1 low). One produces no coordinate (win-community-center, Windham CT) and one is low precision (cedar-lake, anchored to Cedar Pond Road rather than the recreation area — repair-pass class 1a, needing a better ANCHOR rather than a better address). Every miss is a genuine HTTP 200 with an empty result set, not rate limiting: scripts/lib/geocode-nominatim.mjs throws on any non-200. Set false so these import as gate-blocked drafts in the work queue (the Little Rock precedent) instead of aborting the metro. This is the best-converting metro in wave 1 at 18/24 projected publish, and geography is barely a factor — 4 of its 6 held rows are held on the evidence bar.
_reconcile_comment: ONE RECONCILE, SURFACED BY PRE-FLIGHT AT THE CANDIDATES STAGE — the projection stage could not have caught it, because project reads the artifact and this is a collision with a row already in the database. PickleballU (Sturbridge) already exists as a dormant OSM draft, so an INSERT would have produced a duplicate venue and a slug collision on `pickleballu-sturbridge-ma`. Reconcile as an UPDATE keyed on osm_id, never an INSERT; osm_id is preserved and the OSM original is stashed in provenance.osm_reconcile.osm_original, so ODbL lineage carries forward. UNLIKE Toledo's Pickle Zone (deferred because the workbook and the OSM row DISAGREED on access_type, where guessing would write a wrong access class to a live page), THIS PAIR DOES NOT CONFLICT: both say access_type='public', and the research row only ADDS facts the OSM row lacked (fee_type='fee', court_count=6, indoor=true, a tier-1 controlling-entity source). Identity is not inferred from proximity alone — the research row's own independent geocode resolved to the exact same OSM node, node/11632384135, at 0 m, with the same name and the same generated slug. The Syracuse erie-canal reconcile is the direct precedent. The other live listing inside this envelope, The Millworks (Westford MA), is NOT a conflict and is deliberately untouched: Westford is in Middlesex County, outside the Worcester MSA, and sits in the box only because an envelope is a rectangle.

reconciles.note: SAME venue as the dormant OSM row. The research row's own geocode anchored to this exact OSM node (leisure/sports_hall node/11632384135 "PickleballU") at 0 m, and both rows generate the identical slug pickleballu-sturbridge-ma. No field conflicts: the OSM row is access_type='public' and the research row agrees; fee_type, court_count, indoor and the controlling-entity source are all additive. The address refines from the OSM row's '178 Main Street' to the venue's own '178C Main St' (unit-level, from pickleballu.com, tier 1).

_expected_publish_comment: RE-AUTHORED 2026-08-05 from the confirming --stage=project run under the CURRENT gate, approved by the owner. The previous block (count 18) was locked 2026-08-03 against the pre-ADR-16/17 gate — 4 of its 6 hold reasons were 'research_status=probable' and one was 'coordinate precision low', both retired as gate conditions. It was REPLACED, not edited to match output: the block was removed, the projection was run with no expectation present, and this was written from what it printed. rt-12-pickle is a NEW hold that did not exist under the old gate, and it is a FALSE POSITIVE that the owner has deliberately accepted for this release: isGenericName() strips 'pickle' as a noise word and then strips the digits, leaving 'rt' — two characters — so a tier-1-sourced, research_status='verified', high-precision commercial venue with its own website reads as unnamed. Measured across all 1,354 venues in every metro artifact the rule produces exactly TWO such false positives (this and memphis's 'Pickleball 901') while correctly blocking 76 raw OSM drafts named things like '1', '2' and 'Pickleball Court'. Renaming the venue would put a false name in the directory permanently; widening the rule is correct but belongs in its own slice against the ADR-17 shared module, where publish-facilities.mjs re-evaluates it against live rows. Worcester ships 22 and this row is released by that later slice.
